title: Sappho 31 erratum chain: the hanging line, the Philo battery and Josephus
description: These historical theses, mostly from the erratum chain and the Ω erratum, read Sappho 31 as an operative structure of collapse, inscription and survival carried through later texts. The hanging line is a completed open form that Longinus quotes as whole, the Peri Hypsous is the headless document holding Sappho and Moses in one hand, and Philo's Quis Heres 249-266 and canonical Josephus carry the poem's apparatus without her name, with the chain extended to Diotima and Revelation. Unbuilt tests include the Philo blind-reconstruction battery with near-miss controls, a survey of which constraints were already portable, and the pre-registered Qurʾanic frozen operator test.

claims.statement: Longinus quotes the four surviving stanzas of Sappho 31 as his exemplar of sublimity. He does not indicate that he is quoting an incomplete poem. He treats the four-stanza-plus-hanging-line unit as complete for his purpose. Under the documentary framing, this is a puzzle — why does Longinus not remark on the poem's incompleteness? Under the hanging-line framing, the puzzle dissolves. The four stanzas plus the hanging line *are* complete as a compositional unit. The completion by continuation is the reader's or performer's participation. Longinus is quoting the poem's own presentation of itself, which is not a truncation but a resolved openness.

claims.statement: For roughly two centuries, the mainstream editorial tradition has treated the fifth-stanza opening as marginal to the poem's body. Popular translations often omit it entirely; anthology editions frequently print only the four stanzas; scholarly editions typically include the opening but often relegate it to reduced type or to critical apparatus. The distinction matters. The reading public — including undergraduates working from anthologies, poets encountering the poem in translation, and general readers of introductory volumes — has often received "Sappho 31" as a four-stanza poem ending at *φαίνομ᾽ ἔμ᾽ αὔτᾳ*.

claims.registered_title: The Queen's Seizure and the Re-fired King: Sappho 31 in Canonical Josephus
claims.statement: The Sappho-in-Josephus hypothesis has until now rested on two supports of unequal and contested weight: material in the Slavonic Josephus, whose textual authority is disputed, and a fully conjectural location in Revelation. This paper moves the claim onto the uncontested Greek corpus. Two loci in canonical Josephus realize the fr. 31 apparatus in complementary polarity — Antiquities 11.234–241 forward, Bellum 1.436–444 inverted — and a six-occurrence verb stitches them at the reactivation joint. The Slavonic and Revelation locations are hereby reframed: not freestanding conjecture, but extensions of an attested intra-corpus pattern.
